# M001/S01 — RetroDiffusion evaluation (2026-09-05)

Full evaluation: `.gsd/reports/m001-s01-testgen/EVALUATION.md` (capabilities, style shortlist, measured costs, test generation, pipeline design).

## Verdict
**ADOPT** RetroDiffusion as primary pixel-art source for characters (recorded in DECISIONS).

## Key numbers
- Test gen: rd_pro__default 104x104 x2 = $0.36; both variants Habbo-viable (big head, small body, transparent, clean pixels)
- 48px path: ~$0.86/character; 104px path: ~$3.21/character; balance ~$8.85
- Exact legacy-format match: rd_animation__four_angle_walking_idle (48x48, 4-dir walk+idle)
- 8-dir: rd_animation__8_dir_rotation (80x80, supports reference images)

## Pipeline design
RD hosted URLs -> download to assets/rd/<name>/ -> adapted pack script (same manifest contract) -> esbuild dist -> renderer (frame-size calibration in S02).

## S02 starting point
48px parity first (cheapest), then 104px PixelLab-parity composition.

# S02: Implement: RD generation -> pack -> render pipeline

**Milestone:** M001
**Slice:** S02

**Goal:** Generate a character with RetroDiffusion at 48px, pack it into the existing spritesheet+manifest contract (pl_rot_N / pl_idle_N_F / pl_walk_N_F, Texture Packer JSON), and wire it into the renderer - proving the RD pipeline end to end.
**Demo:** A new character spritesheet (e.g. habbo_inspiration_new successor) generated with RetroDiffusion, packed via the updated script, and the avatar walking in the Habbo room at the correct scale.

## Must-Haves

- 1) Pack script consumes RD outputs and emits the renderer contract. 2) One RD character covering 8 directions with walk+idle. 3) Manifest validation passes (key counts, cell size, sheet dims). 4) Avatar visible in the room and walking at the right scale. 5) Generation spend logged.

## Proof Level

- This slice proves: runtime

## Integration Closure

Renderer serves the RD-packed character at runtime; legacy M007/S02 renderer-calibration scope absorbed (48px first; 104px calibration deferred).

## Verification

- Pack script logs key counts and dimensions; generation spend logged.

<tasks>
- [ ] **T01**: Generate RD 48px character assets _(small)_
  Base character (rd_pro__default 48x48), 4-dir walk+idle set (four_angle_walking_idle), mirrored to 8 Habbo directions. Log generation spend.
  - Files: `assets/rd/eval-char/`
  - Verify: Assets downloaded, visually inspected, spend recorded against balance.
- [ ] **T02**: Write pack-rd-sprites.mjs _(medium)_
  Cut RD sheets into a Texture Packer atlas + pl_* manifest (8 rot, 32 idle, 48 walk frames); mirror 4 dirs; pad walk to 6 frames if RD yields 4.
  - Files: `scripts/pack-rd-sprites.mjs`
  - Verify: node scripts/pack-rd-sprites.mjs ... then JSON key-count check (88 frames, cell 48x48).
- [ ] **T03**: Wire atlas into the app and verify in-app _(small)_
  Point the pixellab atlas at the RD-packed sheet (backing up the original), build, restart web server, confirm avatar walks at correct scale.
  - Files: `src/web/main.tsx`
  - Verify: In-app: avatar walks correctly; manifest served from dist.
</tasks>

## Files Likely Touched

- assets/rd/eval-char/
- scripts/pack-rd-sprites.mjs
- src/web/main.tsx

# M001: RetroDiffusion as Primary Pixel-Art Source

**Vision:** Make RetroDiffusion the primary source of truth for generated pixel-art assets (characters first), replacing the currently-unavailable PixelLab pipeline. Plan first - evaluate capabilities, cost, style fit, and design the generation->pack->render pipeline - then implement it separately: adapt the packing scripts to RD output format, generate and pack a real character, and wire it into the renderer (absorbing the pending legacy M007/S02 "wire into renderer & calibrate" scope).

## Success Criteria

- A recorded adopt/reject decision for RetroDiffusion as primary pixel-art source, backed by capability + cost evidence
- A documented pipeline design (generation -> packing -> manifest -> renderer)
- One character generated via RetroDiffusion, packed, and rendering in the room with correct walk/idle at calibrated scale
- Legacy M007/S02 scope (wire into renderer & calibrate) closed under the new pipeline

## Slices

- [ ] **S01: Plan: RetroDiffusion as primary pixel-art source** `risk:low` `depends:[]`
  > After this: A decision record in GSD DECISIONS plus a short pipeline design note: which RD styles/sizes to use for characters, expected cost per character set, and the flow RD output -> assets/ -> renderer.

- [ ] **S02: Implement: RD generation -> pack -> render pipeline** `risk:medium` `depends:[S01]`
  > After this: A new character spritesheet (e.g. habbo_inspiration_new successor) generated with RetroDiffusion, packed via the updated script, and the avatar walking in the Habbo room at the correct scale.

## Boundary Map

| In scope | Out of scope |
|---|---|
| RetroDiffusion as primary source for character sprites (generation -> packing -> renderer) | Migrating existing furniture pipeline off PixelLab naming |
| Adaptation of pack-pixellab-sprites.mjs (or successor) to RD output format | Regenerating already-packed furniture assets |
| Legacy M007/S02 renderer calibration for non-48px frames | New avatar features beyond walk/idle |
| Decision record + pipeline design doc | Bulk regeneration of all legacy characters (follow-up) |

# M002: Restore Original Habbo Figure Avatar System

**Vision:** Restore the Nitro multi-layer Habbo figure avatar system from git history (deleted in 17.8 for copyright): authentic 8-direction walks via 5 sprite directions + mirrors, layered body-part composition with outfit tinting, sitting, blinking, and the sprite-sheet debug grid. Figure assets are downloaded locally per dev machine and gitignored (never committed), matching the furniture asset posture that survived 17.8. The PixelLab/RD single-sprite renderer stays as the fallback when figure assets are absent.

## Success Criteria

- Agents render as original Habbo figures with authentic 8-direction walking (no perspective breaks)
- Restored figure renderer + outfit config tests pass in the current codebase
- Figure assets download locally, gitignored, never committed (verified)
- AvatarDebugGrid (sprite-sheet debug view) restored and reachable
- PixelLab/RD renderer remains the fallback when figure assets are absent

## Slices

- [ ] **S01: Recover & adapt figure renderer code** `risk:medium` `depends:[]`
  > After this: Figure renderer module + outfit config compile in-tree with restored tests passing under vitest (no in-app wiring yet).

- [ ] **S02: Restore figure asset pipeline (local-only assets)** `risk:low` `depends:[S01]`
  > After this: Running the download script fetches figure assets into assets/habbo/ (local only), converts to Nitro sprites, and the manifest lists figures; git status stays clean of figure files.

- [ ] **S03: Wire figure renderer into the room + debug grid** `risk:medium` `depends:[S01,S02]`
  > After this: Agents in localhost:3000 render as original Habbo figures, walking in all 8 directions with correct perspective; debug grid viewable for the figure atlas.

## Boundary Map

| In scope | Out of scope |
|---|---|
| isoAvatarRenderer + avatarOutfitConfig restore from 586772b^ | AvatarBuilderModal/builder UI (follow-up) |
| Figure asset download pipeline (local-only, gitignored) | Committing any figure assets (never) |

# S02: Failure-mode hardening: bootstrap, event bus, surfaced degradation

**Milestone:** M003
**Slice:** S02

**Goal:** Fix demonstrated failure classes: one shared asset-bootstrap module for both hosts, typed event bus with startup replay, surfaced degradation in the status chip.
**Demo:** Demo page with the network tab throttled: no lost cards; a degraded board fetch shows a visible indicator; both loaders share one bootstrap module (diff shows deletion of duplicated code).

## Must-Haves

- 1) Single asset-bootstrap; duplicate loaders deleted. 2) Bus replay: dispatch-before-listener survives (regression tested). 3) Degraded states visible (chip segments: board source, figures, warning count). 4) Suite green; healthy paths unchanged.

## Proof Level

- This slice proves: runtime

## Integration Closure

Web + extension boot paths share the bootstrap; demo and live both exercise replay.

## Verification

- Status chip segments; bootstrap report logs; degradation registry.

  - Verify: tests/bus.test.ts (8 tests incl. dispatch-before-listener survival).

  - Files: `src/assetBootstrap.ts`, `src/web/main.tsx`, `src/webview.tsx`

# S03: Render layer pipeline: formalize room, notes, and dynamic layers

**Milestone:** M003
**Slice:** S03

**Goal:** Generalize the Q12/Q13 render-layer pattern into an explicit WorldLayer pipeline, extracted out of RoomCanvas into a CanvasStage module; module-level mutable renderer state becomes stage-owned.
**Demo:** CanvasStage owns canvas+layers; RoomCanvas shrank by the extracted code; pan/zoom/walk performance not worse (measured render cadence); behavior identical.

## Must-Haves

- 1) src/render/CanvasStage.ts owns canvas lifecycle + input + frame loop (no resize/wheel/touch listeners in RoomCanvas). 2) src/render/layers.ts WorldLayer contract + RoomLayer/NotesLayer migrations. 3) isoKanbanRenderer module-level mutable state eliminated. 4) Frame scheduler formalized + render/skip counters. 5) RoomCanvas >=25% smaller; cadence measured; suite 547/547.

## Proof Level

- This slice proves: runtime

## Integration Closure

All world-space drawing flows through the layer pipeline; renderers keep pure draw functions.

## Verification

- Render/skip counters via dev accessor.

<tasks>
- [ ] **T01**: Extract CanvasStage (canvas lifecycle + input + loop) _(large)_
  Move canvas init/resize, camera state, pointer/wheel/touch input, and the rAF frame loop out of RoomCanvas into src/render/CanvasStage.ts; RoomCanvas instantiates it.
  - Files: `src/render/CanvasStage.ts`, `src/RoomCanvas.tsx`
  - Verify: no resize/wheel/touch listeners remain in RoomCanvas; suite green.
- [ ] **T02**: WorldLayer contract + RoomLayer/NotesLayer _(medium)_
  src/render/layers.ts: WorldLayer (invalidation inputs, render, visible-slice blit); migrate room buffer + notes cache behind it; buffer state moves into the stage.
  - Files: `src/render/layers.ts`, `src/RoomCanvas.tsx`
  - Verify: layers blit identically; no offscreen fields left on RoomCanvas renderState.
- [ ] **T03**: Scheduler + counters + module-state elimination _(medium)_
  Formalize the throttle in CanvasStage with render/skip counters; move isoKanbanRenderer hit-area/rect module state into stage-owned per-render structures.
  - Files: `src/render/CanvasStage.ts`, `src/isoKanbanRenderer.ts`, `src/RoomCanvas.tsx`
  - Verify: counters observed; no module-level mutable state remains in isoKanbanRenderer.
- [ ] **T04**: RoomCanvas slim-down + perf evidence _(small)_
  RoomCanvas keeps heightmap/agents/kanban data wiring; measure idle + pan cadence before/after and document in the PR.
  - Files: `src/RoomCanvas.tsx`
  - Verify: RoomCanvas >=25% smaller; cadence no regression; suite 547/547.
</tasks>

## Files Likely Touched

- src/render/CanvasStage.ts
- src/RoomCanvas.tsx
- src/render/layers.ts
- src/isoKanbanRenderer.ts

# M003: Refactor: Architecture Map, Failure-Mode Hardening, Render Layers, State Store

**Vision:** Make the current architecture visible, harden the places that demonstrably go wrong, and formalize the patterns that emerged ad hoc during feature work. Deliver an honest architecture map (module graph, data flow, render pipeline, event flow) as living docs; extract the canvas/asset/bootstrap concerns out of the 1,882-line RoomCanvas; turn the ad-hoc render-layer caches into an explicit layer pipeline; consolidate app state (agents, cards, camera, demo-vs-live) behind a typed store with explicit invalidation. Keep the room pixel-perfect and fast throughout (536-test suite + visual UAT as guardrails).

## Success Criteria

- Living architecture docs (generated module graph + hand-annotated data flow, render pipeline, event lifecycle, asset pipeline) committed and regenerable
- Failure-mode inventory: every known incident mapped to root cause, guard, and residual risk
- Single asset-bootstrap for web + extension; typed event bus with startup replay; degraded states visible in UI
- CanvasStage + WorldLayer pipeline extracted from RoomCanvas; module-level renderer state eliminated
- Typed app-state store with explicit demo/live mode machine; WS reconnect regression-tested
- Suite green throughout; pan/zoom/idle render cadence not regressed (measured)

## Slices

- [ ] **S01: Architecture visualization + honest current-state map** `risk:low` `depends:[]`
  > After this: docs/architecture/ with mermaid diagrams (module graph generated via madge, hand-annotated data-flow + render-pipeline + event-lifecycle diagrams), plus a documented failure-mode inventory with the concrete incidents that demonstrated each (canvas sizing races, demo event lost pre-listener, silent fallbacks, typecheck .tsx gap).

- [ ] **S02: Failure-mode hardening: bootstrap, event bus, surfaced degradation** `risk:medium` `depends:[S01]`
  > After this: Demo page with the network tab throttled: no lost cards; a degraded board fetch shows a visible indicator; both loaders share one bootstrap module (diff shows deletion of duplicated code).

- [ ] **S03: Render layer pipeline: formalize room, notes, and dynamic layers** `risk:medium` `depends:[S01]`
  > After this: CanvasStage owns canvas+layers; RoomCanvas shrank by the extracted code; pan/zoom/walk performance not worse (measured render cadence); behavior identical.

- [ ] **S04: Typed app-state store: agents, cards, camera, mode** `risk:medium` `depends:[S03]`
  > After this: WS drop + reconnect: agents clear/repopulate via store transitions; demo fallback triggers via an explicit mode transition; kanban filter/notes invalidation flows through store subscriptions.

- [ ] **S05: Live board updates: webhook pub-sub with ETag-probe fallback** `risk:medium` `depends:[S02]`
  > After this: Edit the board -> wall updates within ~1-2s (webhook mode) or ~10s (probe mode), measured. Status chip shows the active board source.

- [ ] **S06: Hosted backend deployment: live wall + agents on a public URL** `risk:medium` `depends:[S02,S05]`
  > After this: A public URL serving the room: board edits reflect in ~1-2s via webhook; Copilot-sourced agents visible; demo fallback when no token configured.

- [ ] **S07: Investigation: agent hooks for role-specific deterministic automation** `risk:low` `depends:[]`
  > After this: docs/agent-hooks/INVESTIGATION.md with surface inventory, role x hook matrix, prototype results, and verdict; two working prototype scripts under scripts/hooks/.

## Boundary Map

| In scope | Out of scope |
|---|---|
| RoomCanvas decomposition (CanvasStage, layer pipeline) | Avatar builder UI (separate follow-up) |
| Shared asset bootstrap + typed event bus + replay | New features on the room (visual changes) |
| Typed app-state store (agents/cards/mode/camera) | Changing asset formats or the RD/PixelLab pipelines |
| Failure-mode inventory + degraded-state surfacing | Rewriting renderers (draw functions stay, signatures may widen) |

slices.goal: Decide and document whether RetroDiffusion becomes the primary source of truth for generated pixel-art assets, with a concrete pipeline design for how its outputs flow into assets/ and the renderer.
slices.success_criteria: 1) Capability comparison RetroDiffusion vs PixelLab documented (8-direction rotations, walk/idle cycles, transparency, per-style size limits relevant to 48px/104px targets). 2) Cost model: estimated spend per full character set (turnaround + 8-dir rotation + walk/idle) using estimate_inference_cost. 3) Candidate RD styles shortlisted for the Habbo look. 4) Decision (adopt/reject RD as primary source) recorded via gsd_decision_save. 5) Pipeline design note written: how RD output (hosted URLs/base64) reaches assets/, manifest format compatibility with pack-pixellab-sprites.mjs, and what changes in the pack script.
slices.integration_closure: Decision + design recorded via GSD (decision_save, summary_save) so the implementation slice executes against a written contract, not chat context.
slices.observability_impact: Cost-per-generation and balance checks surfaced in planning notes; no runtime observability changes.

slices.title: Implement: RD generation -> pack -> render pipeline
slices.demo: A new character spritesheet (e.g. habbo_inspiration_new successor) generated with RetroDiffusion, packed via the updated script, and the avatar walking in the Habbo room at the correct scale.
slices.goal: Generate a character with RetroDiffusion at 48px, pack it into the existing spritesheet+manifest contract (pl_rot_N / pl_idle_N_F / pl_walk_N_F, Texture Packer JSON), and wire it into the renderer - proving the RD pipeline end to end.
slices.success_criteria: 1) Pack script consumes RD outputs and emits the renderer contract. 2) One RD character covering 8 directions with walk+idle. 3) Manifest validation passes (key counts, cell size, sheet dims). 4) Avatar visible in the room and walking at the right scale. 5) Generation spend logged.
slices.integration_closure: Renderer serves the RD-packed character at runtime; legacy M007/S02 renderer-calibration scope absorbed (48px first; 104px calibration deferred).
slices.observability_impact: Pack script logs key counts and dimensions; generation spend logged.

slices.title: Recover & adapt figure renderer code
slices.demo: Figure renderer module + outfit config compile in-tree with restored tests passing under vitest (no in-app wiring yet).
slices.goal: Recover isoAvatarRenderer.ts, avatarOutfitConfig.ts, and their tests from git history (586772b^) and adapt them to the current codebase so the figure renderer compiles and its unit tests pass alongside the PixelLab renderer.
slices.success_criteria: 1) Renderer + outfit config restored, typecheck-clean (0 new errors). 2) Restored tests adapted and passing. 3) Coexists via AvatarRenderer interface, no runtime wiring. 4) No figure assets committed.
slices.integration_closure: Renderer is an in-tree AvatarRenderer implementation; runtime selection deferred to S03.

slices.title: Restore figure asset pipeline (local-only assets)
slices.demo: Running the download script fetches figure assets into assets/habbo/ (local only), converts to Nitro sprites, and the manifest lists figures; git status stays clean of figure files.
slices.goal: Restore the figure download/conversion pipeline from git history: figure loop in scripts/download-habbo-assets.mjs, figure section in scripts/convert-cortex-to-nitro.mjs, esbuild copy step, and manifest figures array - with all downloaded figure assets gitignored and never committed.
slices.success_criteria: 1) download-habbo-assets.mjs figure loop restored (cortex-assets source). 2) convert-cortex-to-nitro.mjs figure section restored. 3) esbuild copies habbo figure assets to dist (gitignored paths only). 4) .gitignore covers figure assets; git check-ignore verified. 5) Figure sprite keys (h_std_/h_wlk_ per part/dir/frame) loadable via spriteCache Nitro path.
slices.integration_closure: Asset pipeline produces exactly the sprite keys the S01 renderer requests; verified by a load check.
slices.observability_impact: Download script logs fetched asset counts.

slices.title: Wire figure renderer into the room + debug grid
slices.demo: Agents in localhost:3000 render as original Habbo figures, walking in all 8 directions with correct perspective; debug grid viewable for the figure atlas.
slices.goal: Select the Habbo figure renderer at runtime when figure assets are available (fallback to pixelLab otherwise), restore AvatarDebugGrid as the sprite-sheet debug tool, and verify authentic 8-direction walking in the room.
slices.success_criteria: 1) Renderer selection: figure assets present -> habboRenderer, absent -> pixelLabRenderer (fallback verified both ways). 2) Avatar walks in all 8 directions with authentic perspective (5 sprites + mirrors, no perspective breaks). 3) AvatarDebugGrid restored and reachable (dev view of the full figure sheet). 4) Idle (std + blink) and sitting states work. 5) Full test suite green.
slices.integration_closure: Room render pipeline serves figure avatars end to end; legacy figure system scope fully closed under current architecture.
slices.observability_impact: Renderer selection logged at startup (which avatar system is active).

slices.title: Architecture visualization + honest current-state map
slices.demo: docs/architecture/ with mermaid diagrams (module graph generated via madge, hand-annotated data-flow + render-pipeline + event-lifecycle diagrams), plus a documented failure-mode inventory with the concrete incidents that demonstrated each (canvas sizing races, demo event lost pre-listener, silent fallbacks, typecheck .tsx gap).
slices.goal: Generate and commit living architecture documentation that shows how the system REALLY works today: module dependency graph, runtime data flow (WS/events -> store -> render loop -> layers), asset pipeline (download/convert/pack/dist), render-layer pipeline, and an event/message flow map including timing-sensitive spots.
slices.success_criteria: 1) docs/architecture/ committed: module graph (generated), data-flow, render-pipeline, event-lifecycle, asset-pipeline diagrams. 2) Failure-mode inventory table: symptom, root cause, current guard, residual risk. 3) Diagrams regenerate via one npm script. 4) Each claim traceable to a real incident or code location.
slices.integration_closure: Docs committed and linked from README; diagrams referenced by later slices as the refactor target state.

slices.title: Failure-mode hardening: bootstrap, event bus, surfaced degradation
slices.demo: Demo page with the network tab throttled: no lost cards; a degraded board fetch shows a visible indicator; both loaders share one bootstrap module (diff shows deletion of duplicated code).
slices.goal: Fix the demonstrated failure classes at their root: (a) extract a single asset-bootstrap module used by BOTH web and extension loaders (kill the duplicated 7-call loaders), (b) make the extensionMessage event bus lifecycle-safe (typed dispatch, listener-ready gate or replay buffer so early events like demo cards cannot be lost), (c) surface silent degradation (11 return-[] sites) as observable states instead of console-only warnings.
slices.success_criteria: 1) One asset-bootstrap module; web + extension loaders call it (duplicated loader code deleted). 2) Event bus: typed emit/on with startup replay (or attach-before-dispatch guarantee) + test proving a demo kanbanCards dispatch survives listener attachment timing. 3) Degraded data states visible in UI (e.g. status chip: board source live/demo/degraded). 4) Full suite green; no behavior change in healthy paths.
slices.integration_closure: Web + extension boot paths verified; demo and live agent paths both exercise the replay guarantee.
slices.observability_impact: Degraded-state chip in the status bar; bootstrap logs aggregated.

slices.title: Render layer pipeline: formalize room, notes, and dynamic layers
slices.demo: CanvasStage owns canvas+layers; RoomCanvas shrank by the extracted code; pan/zoom/walk performance not worse (measured render cadence); behavior identical.
slices.goal: Generalize the Q12/Q13 render-layer pattern into an explicit WorldLayer pipeline, extracted out of RoomCanvas into a CanvasStage module; module-level mutable renderer state becomes stage-owned.
slices.success_criteria: 1) src/render/CanvasStage.ts owns canvas lifecycle + input + frame loop (no resize/wheel/touch listeners in RoomCanvas). 2) src/render/layers.ts WorldLayer contract + RoomLayer/NotesLayer migrations. 3) isoKanbanRenderer module-level mutable state eliminated. 4) Frame scheduler formalized + render/skip counters. 5) RoomCanvas >=25% smaller; cadence measured; suite 547/547.
slices.integration_closure: All world-space drawing flows through the layer pipeline; renderers keep pure draw functions.

slices.title: Typed app-state store: agents, cards, camera, mode
slices.demo: WS drop + reconnect: agents clear/repopulate via store transitions; demo fallback triggers via an explicit mode transition; kanban filter/notes invalidation flows through store subscriptions.
slices.goal: Consolidate scattered app state (kanbanCardsRef, orchStateRef, agent statuses, demo-vs-live flag, camera) behind a small typed store with explicit update/subscribe semantics that feeds the frame scheduler — replacing per-ref ad-hoc mutation and the implicit 5s demo fallback timer with an explicit mode state machine (booting -> live / demo).
slices.success_criteria: 1) Typed store modules (agents, kanban, mode) with update + subscribe; RoomCanvas/overlay read via subscriptions. 2) Demo-vs-live is an explicit store state machine; the 5s fallback is a transition, not a timer side-effect. 3) WS reconnect semantics preserved (clearAgents path) with a regression test. 4) Suite green; visual behavior unchanged.
slices.integration_closure: Render loop consumes store snapshots; no direct ref mutation outside the store for migrated state.

slices.title: Live board updates: webhook pub-sub with ETag-probe fallback
slices.demo: Edit the board -> wall updates within ~1-2s (webhook mode) or ~10s (probe mode), measured. Status chip shows the active board source.
slices.goal: Replace the fixed 60s kanban poll with event-driven board updates: webhook receiver (GitHub projects_v2_item, ADO service hooks) as the live path, conditional ETag updatedAt probe (~10s, 304s rate-limit-free) as fallback; full fetch only on change. Source surfaced per S02.
slices.success_criteria: 1) Webhook endpoint (HMAC validated, projects_v2_item + ADO service hooks) with debounce + full fetch + broadcast. 2) Conditional probe source with If-None-Match at ~10s. 3) BoardSource port: webhook | probe | demo. 4) Measured wall latency per mode. 5) Suite green.
slices.integration_closure: BoardSource feeds the same typed bus as agents (S02); extension keeps polling (documented).
slices.observability_impact: Probe 304/200 log, webhook receipts, board-source status chip.

slices.title: Hosted backend deployment: live wall + agents on a public URL
slices.demo: A public URL serving the room: board edits reflect in ~1-2s via webhook; Copilot-sourced agents visible; demo fallback when no token configured.
slices.goal: Package and document deploying the web-server (room + WS + webhook receiver + board sources) to a public host: Dockerfile (Node 22), env contract (GITHUB_TOKEN, WEBHOOK_SECRET, project config, Copilot monitor token), webhook registration helper, health endpoint, and a deployment guide. Enables a fully live hosted wall (board edits in ~1-2s) viewable from any device. Local JSONL agent watching is local-only by design; hosted agents come from the Copilot monitor.
slices.success_criteria: 1) Dockerfile + compose/fly config; container runs web-server on Node 22. 2) Env contract documented + .env.example; secrets never committed. 3) Webhook registration helper script (creates repo webhook with public URL + secret). 4) /health endpoint. 5) Deployment guide (docs/guides/deploy-live-backend.md) with platform notes (VPS+Docker default, Fly example). 6) Measured: webhook latency ~1-2s on the deployed instance; demo fallback works without tokens. 7) Suite green.
slices.integration_closure: Hosted instance exercises the same BoardSource + bus as local; status chip shows webhook-live mode.
slices.observability_impact: Health endpoint; startup logs list active board source + registered capabilities.

slices.title: Investigation: agent hooks for role-specific deterministic automation
slices.demo: docs/agent-hooks/INVESTIGATION.md with surface inventory, role x hook matrix, prototype results, and verdict; two working prototype scripts under scripts/hooks/.
slices.goal: Investigate the usefulness of agent hooks (deterministic automations on agent lifecycle events) for the distinct agent roles in this project: room-visualized team agents (planning/core-dev/infrastructure/support), GSD workflow roles (planner/executor/reviewer), and GitHub Copilot agent roles (asset-pipeline, visual-regression). Inventory available hook surfaces (Claude Code hooks incl. existing user config, Mault detectors, GSD event stream, agent JSONL transcripts, git hooks, GitHub Actions), map role x hook value, prototype the two highest-value hooks, and record an adopt/defer verdict per role.
slices.success_criteria: 1) Surface inventory verified on this machine (what each can observe/do). 2) Role x hook matrix with value ratings. 3) Two prototypes demonstrating the top data paths. 4) Verdict per role recorded (GSD decision). 5) Recommendation: which hooks become follow-up slices.
slices.integration_closure: Findings feed the failure-mode inventory (hooks as enforcement for the F-class guards).
slices.observability_impact: Prototype hooks may log structured events.

decisions.decision: Primary source of truth for generated character sprites
decisions.choice: Adopt RetroDiffusion (rd_pro__default + animation styles) as the primary generation source; PixelLab archived. Pack-script manifest format retained as the renderer contract.
decisions.rationale: PixelLab is unavailable; RetroDiffusion is live with reference-image consistency, an exact 48px walk+idle style matching the legacy pack format, 8-dir rotation sets, per-frame advanced animations, free cost estimation, and measured Habbo-viable output quality (test generation 2026-09-05, $0.36). Cost: ~$0.86/char at 48px parity, ~$3.21/char at 104px parity.
decisions.revisable: Revisit if PixelLab returns or RD quality degrades; 48px-first S02 proof may reshape the 104px composition strategy.

decisions.decision: Adopt composite target architecture: hexagonal boundaries + unidirectional typed store + immediate-mode layered renderer, organized by feature slice
decisions.choice: core/ (typed stores: agents, cards, camera, mode), render/ (CanvasStage + WorldLayers, pure draw fns), adapters/ (ws-client, extension-bridge, demo-driver), assets/, integrations/, hosts/. Rejected: ECS, Clean/Onion ceremony, event sourcing.
decisions.rationale: Each piece formalizes an existing half-pattern with demonstrated failure evidence: 3 data sources already converge on one event bus (hexagonal), scattered refs caused the sizing/timing bugs (store), Q12/Q13 invented WorldLayer+invalidation caches ad hoc (immediate-mode layers). Guardrails: 536 tests + perf cadence measurements.
decisions.revisable: Revisit if the room grows real simulation (ECS reconsidered) or team size justifies heavier layering.

decisions.decision: Adopt agent hooks for the GSD executor/reviewer roles and the asset-pipeline role; defer visualization-role and Mault-style detectors
decisions.choice: Prototypes validated (scripts/hooks/gsd-event-hook.mjs + room-tool-feed.mjs): GSD event-log tail reacts to planner/executor/reviewer commands; Claude Code PostToolUse hook tags tool activity by AGENT_ROLE with role-specific triggers. Both feed .gsd/hooks-feed.jsonl (append-only, gitignored). Adoption slice next: wire feed -> web-server WS -> status chip, project-level .claude/settings.json hooks, gate-evidence automation for milestones.
decisions.rationale: Deterministic hooks remove manual steps performed repeatedly this week (issue evidence comments, pack+build after asset changes, milestone gate evidence collection). Surfaces already exist and half are active (Claude Code hooks run gsd-check-update/gsd-context-monitor; GSD event log is structured and ordered). Low risk: prototypes are read+append-only.
decisions.revisable: Revisit visual-regression/infrastructure hooks after S06 (hosted backend); revisit Mault if hook complexity outgrows Claude Code hooks.

decisions.when_context: gsd-loop trial #84/PR #85 completed 2026-09-09; M003 S03-S06 pending
decisions.decision: Route M003 remaining slices (S03, S04, S05, S06) through the gsd-loop label queue; quick fixes stay direct-dispatch
decisions.choice: Hybrid routing: GSD Pi remains the planning authority (milestone/slice plans, evidence, DECISIONS); each remaining M003 slice ALSO gets a gsd-loop contract issue (canonical ## Outcomes checkbox format) - human applies gsd:ready to release the build lane; builder opens the PR; reviewer posts a pinned verdict; human merges. Quick fixes (Q-style) stay direct-dispatch.
decisions.rationale: Trial #84 validated the loop end-to-end (spec -> gsd:ready -> build -> verdict -> gsd:approved -> merge) with proportionate ceremony for contract-clear slices. Label state machine gives the room a real queue signal (S05 synergy). Human gates at slice release + merge preserve the deterministic-development boundary. GSD Pi keeps depth (evidence, decisions, milestone arcs) while the loop owns execution traffic.
decisions.revisable: Revisit per slice: if a slice contract cannot be written as checkbox outcomes (deep architectural work), route it back to direct dispatch with GSD Pi evidence.
